title: Trampoline Park Tips: Safety, Socks and Best Sessions
description: Trampoline park tips for families: grip socks, waivers, toddler sessions, safety rules, avoiding injuries and how to find quieter, cheaper times to bounce.
intro: Trampoline parks are brilliant for burning off energy, especially on wet days. A few simple rules keep the fun high and the bumps low.
cardText: Grip socks, waivers, toddler sessions and safety rules.

blocks.title: Scout’s bounce rule
blocks.text: One person per trampoline, no double bouncing, and save flips for supervised areas. Most injuries happen when big and small jumpers mix.
points: Sign the waiver online before you arrive

sections.html:
• Most parks require grip socks: reusable ones save buying again.
  • A parent or guardian usually signs a waiver online.
  • Look for toddler, SEN-friendly and teen sessions.

• One jumper per trampoline.
  • Land on your feet. No flips unless it’s a supervised area.
  • Keep little ones away from busy sessions with older jumpers.
  • Empty pockets and remove jewellery.
Weekday and early sessions are often cheaper, and some parks sell multi-visit passes. More ideas in indoor activities and rainy day days out.

faqs.q: Do you need special socks at trampoline parks?
faqs.a: Most trampoline parks require grip socks for safety. Many sell them at the desk, and you can reuse them on later visits.
